author: BBC News
description:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has said US intelligence sharing on deadly Russian missile attacks "works now" after talks with US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff.
 
The meeting in Oslo came after accusations by Kyiv that Washington was withholding key intelligence - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
 
Finnish President Alexander Stubb, who also took part in the talks, said "genuine progress" was made on proposals to achieve peace but gave no details and warned that patience would be needed.
 
Relations between Ukraine and the US have soured in recent weeks to the extent that Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".

description:
The Canadian province of Alberta has voted to reject a plan to hold a binding referendum on independence. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Albertans and all Canadians would move forward together with renewed purpose and high ambition. 

Alberta is at the heart of Canada's oil and gas industry. Separatist campaigners have argued that Alberta could be richer if it were an independent country. This comes amid a trade war with President Donald Trump - who has mused about Canada becoming the 51st US state.

description:
Today, the latest report from the Covid-19 Inquiry found that action to protect the social care sector came too late, with government failings helping create conditions in which the virus could “spread like wildfire” in care homes.

The report describes social care as an “afterthought” in the early pandemic response, highlighting a lack of planning, testing and protective equipment.

Adam is joined by the BBC’s social affairs editor, Alison Holt, to unpack the findings, discuss the impact on families and explore what needs to change to protect people receiving care in a future emergency.

Also, the BBC’s chief anchor in Washington DC, Caitríona Perry, reports on Donald Trump’s visit to Kansas to support Republican senator Roger Marshall in an unexpectedly tight race against Democrat Adam Hamilton. And Ben Chu, from BBC Verify, examines how the US economy is performing under Trump.

description:
Fires, floods, and typhoons - the impact of El Niño is already having a significant impact on global weather patterns.
 
Countries including Indonesia, India and the United States have been experiencing droughts, floods and heatwaves in line with projections about how extreme weather events will be supercharged by the phenomenon.
 
The World Meteorological Agency says the record-breaking El Niño will strengthen further and persist until at least 2027.
 
The BBC looks at the different ways its impact is already being felt around the world.

description:
People in Alberta have voted overwhelmingly to remain part of Canada, projected results suggest, after residents of the western province were asked in a public ballot whether or not they wanted a referendum at a later date on becoming independent.
 
With most votes counted, more than two-thirds of voters had chosen to remain part of the country rather than pursue the referendum, according to Elections Alberta. The outcome was hailed by Prime Minister Mark Carney as "a clear choice" on the part of Albertans.
 
The province's premier said people “voted for a stronger Alberta,” while separatist leader Jeffrey Rath told the BBC his “movement isn’t stopping”.

Police have charged a man over the alleged vehicle attack on Australian MP Helen Haines, who is in critical but stable condition and has reportedly lost a leg.
 
Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury; intentionally causing serious injury; and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official.
 
Police allege the incident, which occurred outside Haines's electoral office in Wangaratta, was targeted.
 
A barber who was at the scene also recounts how bystanders responded "immediately" and helped disarm the alleged attacker.

author: BBC News
description:
Hundreds of teenagers have told the BBC about their fears for the future and that they want more guidance from school on how to get a job.

A survey for the BBC asked 2,000 young people, all aged 13 to 18, about the world of work - and what help they need to secure employment once they leave full-time education.

Some called for more work experience at school and opportunities to improve their communication skills.

They also highlighted concerns about stress management, personal finances and how to apply for jobs.

In England, the government has an ambition to guarantee two weeks of work experience for every young person. However, this opportunity is not available to all teenagers, with more than half of those surveyed telling us they had not done any.

As part of the Teen Summit project by Radio 5 Live and BBC Bitesize, we followed four students from Newcastle - Param, McKenzie, Jasmine and Javaris - as they tried out roles for the first time as part of their work experience placeme
title: What British teenagers really think about their futures | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
Targeted curfews across France contributed to a quiet night after a weekend of riots and looting across the country, the Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has said.
 
Curfews were introduced across parts of central Paris, including Place de la République, where protesters had gathered over the weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area.
 
Earlier Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez admitted police had "lost control" in some cities.
 
Protests first began last month with students demanding better school conditions escalated to take in a broader range of concerns with numbers at demonstrations bolstered by trade unions and various protest groups.
